title: Magnon-induced phononic Chern insulator
authors: Rui-Chang Shen, Yihao Yang, Haoran Xue
abstract: High-frequency artificial phononic crystals offer a low-loss platform compatible with on-chip integration, yet realizing Chern phononic phases at GHz frequencies remains challenging. Here, we propose a magnon-induced phononic Chern insulator in a honeycomb phononic crystal hybridized with ferromagnetic islands at the hexagon centers. A circularly polarized Kittel mode couples to the surrounding phonons with a phase winding, which breaks time-reversal symmetry and opens a full Chern gap. In the large-detuning regime, this mechanism leads to an effective Haldane-type phononic model with magnon-induced complex hopping. By tuning the magnon-phonon interaction, the full hybrid system accesses Chern phases with tunable Chern numbers |C|=1 and |C|=2. The predicted gaps can exceed realistic phonon and magnon linewidths, enabling their observation in GHz acoustic devices. Our work establishes chiral magnon--phonon hybridization as a route to magnetically reconfigurable topological phononics.
summary: This paper proposes using the coupling between magnons and phonons in a honeycomb phononic crystal to engineer a phononic Chern insulator. By breaking time-reversal symmetry via a circularly polarized magnon mode, the system opens a topological gap, allowing for the creation of tunable, non-dissipative edge states. This establishes a route for magnetically reconfigurable topological phononics in GHz acoustic devices.
main_problem: The primary goal is to realize a phononic Chern insulator at high frequencies (GHz) to achieve robust, one-way boundary transport in acoustic devices.
main_result: The study demonstrates that chiral magnon-phonon hybridization can create a topologically gapped phononic Chern phase with tunable Chern numbers (|C|=1 and |C|=2).
method: The analysis involves deriving an effective Hamiltonian using the Schrieffer-Wolff transformation in the large-detuning limit, leading to a Haldane-type model.
model_or_system: The system is a honeycomb phononic crystal hybridized with ferromagnetic islands. The physics is governed by the coupling between lattice phonons and magnons (Kittel mode).
key_observables: Chern numbers (C), topological gaps ($\Delta_1, \Delta_2$), and the existence of chiral edge states.
important_parameters: Magnon-phonon coupling strength ($g$), detuning ($\delta\omega$), and the ability to tune the Chern number by varying these parameters.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the large-detuning approximation ($|\delta\omega| \gg g, t$) and assumes the coupling phase originates from projecting the right-circular Kittel mode.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the honeycomb structure, momentum-space coupling intensity, and bulk band structures showing the Chern numbers and the spatial distribution of edge states.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the full Hamiltonian ($H = H_{ph} + H_m + H_{int}$), derives the effective Hamiltonian ($H_{eff}$) via Schrieffer-Wolff, and then analyzes the resulting Haldane-type model to predict tunable Chern phases.
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete, solid-state platform (acoustic/phononic) for realizing topological phenomena, bridging concepts from magnetism (magnons) and condensed matter topology (Chern insulators) in a potentially observable, high-frequency domain.

Spintronics.note: The paper explicitly studies the coupling between magnons (spin waves) and phonons, which is a direct extension of the concept of coupling magnetic excitations to lattice vibrations, fitting within the broader scope of hybrid spin-lattice systems relevant to spintronics.
